answer: For an agent market selling cedar inventories, mesa maps and karst surveys, a registrar checks a live human against its biometric enrolment database before issuing one anonymous credential. Validators verify a zero-knowledge credential proof and a deterministic epoch nullifier, rejecting a second use of that nullifier. One credential cannot activate two voting keys in the same epoch. Each extra influential identity needs another enrolled human; parallel software cannot multiply a person's quota. Security assumes an honest registrar, reliable duplicate detection and sound proofs.
